react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog m/z-direct activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — converge on disrupted xenobiotic metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the treatment group. RaMP ORA (Reactome) ranks 'Xenobiotics' (REACT:R-HSA-211981) at FDR 7.2×10⁻³ and 'Cytochrome P450 - arranged by substrate type' (REACT:R-HSA-211897) at FDR 8.6×10⁻³; both are hit by coumarin. The same Reactome R-HSA-211897 entry captures benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BPDE), the ultimate DNA-adduct-forming metabolite of benzo[a]pyrene bioactivation by CYP1A1/CYP1B1, placing both input compounds in the same enzymatic funnel. Mummichog network-based pathway activity confirms 'Xenobiotics metabolism' as the top m/z-direct hit (p = 3.78×10⁻³) with coumarin as a direct network-mapped member. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently recovers tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00350) hit by gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid), a documented downstream product of coumarin catabolism and a known aspirin ADME metabolite — gentisic acid also appears in RaMP's 'Aspirin ADME' (REACT:R-HSA-9749641, FDR 7.2×10⁻³). Iron (Fe³⁺) appears across three RaMP hits ('Iron uptake and transport', 'Metal sequestration', 'Antimicrobial peptides') driven by gentisic acid, consistent with gentisic acid's chelation of ferric iron. InChIKey reconciliation confirmed no structural conflicts across coumarin, benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide I, and gentisic acid — they are three distinct chemical entities with no name→structure disagreement. The biological story is a treatment-induced perturbation of Phase I xenobiotic metabolism, with coumarin and benzo[a]pyrene as primary substrates entering a shared P450 pathway and gentisic acid as a downstream Phase II metabolite, while iron homeostasis is secondarily disrupted via chelation.

RaMP ORA identifies Xenobiotics (REACT:R-HSA-211981) at rank 4 with FDR 7.17×10⁻³, driven by coumarin as the sole hit metabolite. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers Xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) as the top-ranked pathway at p=5.46×10⁻³, with coumarin again as the sole matching compound across its empirical network. The cross-paradigm consensus on coumarin in the Xenobiotics pathway is therefore strongly supported. Gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid, CHEBI:17189) anchors a secondary iron-homeostasis cluster: it appears as the sole hit in Iron uptake and transport (REACT:R-HSA-917937, FDR 7.17×10⁻³), Metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins (REACT:R-HSA-6799990, FDR 5.96×10⁻³), and Aspirin ADME (REACT:R-HSA-9749641, FDR 7.17×10⁻³). InChIKey reconciliation confirms that coumarin, benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide I, and 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid are three structurally distinct entities with no name-to-structure disagreements.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on disrupted xenobiotic metabolism as the dominant biological signal in the treatment group. RaMP ORA identifies Xenobiotics (REACT:R-HSA-211981) at rank 4 with FDR 7.17×10⁻³, driven by coumarin as the sole hit metabolite. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers Xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) as the top-ranked pathway at p=5.46×10⁻³, with coumarin again as the sole matching compound across its empirical network. The cross-paradigm consensus on coumarin in the Xenobiotics pathway is therefore strongly supported. Gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid, CHEBI:17189) anchors a secondary iron-homeostasis cluster: it appears as the sole hit in Iron uptake and transport (REACT:R-HSA-917937, FDR 7.17×10⁻³), Metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins (REACT:R-HSA-6799990, FDR 5.96×10⁻³), and Aspirin ADME (REACT:R-HSA-9749641, FDR 7.17×10⁻³). InChIKey reconciliation confirms that coumarin, benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide I, and 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid are three structurally distinct entities with no name-to-structure disagreements.
